title: x509-cert 0.3 and der 0.8 are in pkix-path's public API, which blocks a credible 1.0
description:
pkix-path's public signatures carry RustCrypto types from crates that are still pre-1.0, so their next minor release is a breaking change in PKIX's own API whether or not PKIX changes a line.

The coupling, measured:

  pub fn validate_path(chain: &[Certificate], ...)   -- x509_cert::Certificate
  pub use x509_cert::ext::pkix::constraints::name::NameConstraints
  pub use spki::{AlgorithmIdentifierRef, SubjectPublicKeyInfoRef}
  253 references to x509_cert:: or der:: in pkix-path/src/lib.rs alone

Dependency levels as resolved today. Mixed, and current rather than lagging -- several of these spent a long time as release candidates:

  signature        3.0.0    post-1.0
  ed25519-dalek    3.0.0    post-1.0
  der              0.8.3    pre-1.0
  spki             0.8.1    pre-1.0
  x509-cert        0.3.1    pre-1.0
  rsa              0.10.0   pre-1.0
  p256/p384/p521   0.14.0   pre-1.0
  sha2 / sha1      0.11.1   pre-1.0
  digest           0.11.3   pre-1.0
  elliptic-curve   0.14.3   pre-1.0

So the traits layer has partly graduated while the formats layer has not, and the formats layer is the one in the public API.

Consequence: PKIX cannot credibly publish 1.0 while a 0.x x509-cert appears in its public signatures, because x509-cert 0.4 would force PKIX 2.0 for reasons that have nothing to do with PKIX. A 1.0 is a promise about the API, and this part of the API is not ours to keep.

The existing mitigation does not reach this. IoFailure's DerError newtype exists exactly so 'a future major-version bump in the der crate cannot cascade into a semver break here' (pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs), and that works for an error type. It cannot work for Certificate without owning X.509 parsing.

Options, none cheap:

1. Wait for x509-cert 1.0 and gate PKIX 1.0 on it. Zero work, indefinite timeline, and not in our control. It also leaves every intermediate x509-cert bump as a PKIX breaking release, which is the status quo and is honest as long as PKIX stays pre-1.0.

2. Define PKIX's own certificate handle at the boundary -- an opaque newtype over the DER with accessors -- and keep x509_cert internal. Removes the coupling for good, but it is a large piece of work, it duplicates an accessor surface that x509-cert already provides well, and it argues against the crate's own premise of being thin over the formats layer. It would also make every caller that already holds an x509_cert::Certificate convert.

3. Re-export the upstream crates wholesale (pub use x509_cert; pub use der;) and document that PKIX's semver tracks theirs. Does not remove the break; it makes the break legible and lets consumers name one version. Cheap, honest, and the usual practice in this corner of the ecosystem.

4. Ship 1.0 anyway and accept that an x509-cert minor forces a PKIX major. Defensible for a library whose users are expected to pin, but it makes the 1.0 promise weaker than the number implies.

Recommendation: 3 now, 1 as the gate. Re-exporting costs nothing, removes the version-matching papercut for consumers, and makes the dependency's semver part of the documented contract instead of a surprise. Then let x509-cert 1.0 be an explicit precondition on any 1.0 plan rather than something discovered during it.

Decide and record. Do not reopen at each dependency bump -- that is what this bead is for.

Filed from a question about where RustCrypto sits; no work was done beyond the measurements above.
